title: Tiny-first SDKs: persona-driven micro-scenarios & failure checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
This is a small, tactical playbook for a Tiny-first SDK onramp aimed at 3 minute-to-success goals. Focus is on persona-driven micro-scenarios (what each user actually needs to run in the first 5 minutes), the minimal telemetry contract we require for safe rollouts, and an explicit checklist for common failure modes and recovery steps.

Why tiny-first?
- Most teams abandon complex quickstarts. A 5-minute success path reduces churn and surfaces the smallest set of integration and runtime problems.
- Empowers non-engineering evaluators (PMs, data analysts) to validate SDK behavior and prompt ergonomics.

Target personas and success criteria
1) Frontend Engineer (fast-proof)
   - Success: Run a single web demo, stream tokens to UI, see latency < 300ms for single-turn.
   - Needs: minimal JS sample, CORS hint, error mapping for network vs server.

2) Backend Engineer (secure-run)
   - Success: Server-side call with API key pinned to env, produce deterministic embedding/response.
   - Needs: small Python example, env var template, CI smoke test snippet.

3) Data Scientist (eval-first)
   - Success: Generate embeddings for 10 documents and run a similarity query.
   - Needs: reproducible seed, small notebook sample, perf numbers for batch=1 vs batch=8.

Micro-scenarios (first-run flows)
- 00:00–01:30 Install client & auth
  - npm i @redwood/inference (or pip install redwood-inference)
  - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REDACTED
  - run: redwood --version (or python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)")

- 01:30–03:00 Hello world call
  - JS: fetch('/generate', { body: JSON.stringify({prompt: 'summarize: ...'})}) => render response.stream
  - Python: client.generate(prompt='summarize ...') -> print chunked outputs

- 03:00–05:00 Validate observability & failures
  - Trigger a 401 (unset key) and observe error code mapping.
  - Simulate latency (local proxy delay) and verify streaming fallback or shorter prompt path works.

Minimal telemetry contract (what we collect to ship safe defaults)
- Required fields (telemetry surface, names):
  - event: string (sdk.init, sdk.request.start, sdk.request.end, sdk.error)
  - sdk_version: string
  - model: string (name/version)
  - region: string
  - latency_ms: number (client-observed end-to-end)
  - tokens_requested: number
  - error_class: string (auth, network, quota, model_unavailable)
  - anonymized_prompt_hash: string (sha256 truncated)

Notes: keep payload small, sample at 1% by default for production, allow customers to opt-out. Telemetry contract must be represented in the SDK as an interface (see linked PR) and a feature flag in Console.

Failure modes + triage checklist (quick)
- 401 / auth failure
  - Symptoms: 401 response, SDK throws AuthError, client logs 'invalid key'
  - Triage: confirm env var, confirm project-level keys in Console, check clock skew if signed tokens.
  - Quick fix: rotate key, verify new key with redwood --whoami

- Rate limit / 429
  - Symptoms: 429 responses, 'retry-after' present, sudden throughput drop
  - Triage: check usage dashboard, confirm burst policy on Dedicated, backoff settings in SDK (exponential jitter)
  - Quick fix: enable local batching or switch to a cheaper model variant for degraded capacity

- Streaming stalls / incomplete chunks
  - Symptoms: partial content, client-side hang, missing final end token
  - Triage: inspect connection (proxy, keepalive), check server logs for injection errors, validate chunk encoding.
  - Quick fix: re-request with single-turn prompt, enable fallback non-streaming path in SDK

- Embedding mismatch / nondeterminism
  - Symptoms: similarity drift between runs
  - Triage: check model version pinned, quantization profile, tokenization differences (unicode normalizations)
  - Quick fix: pin exact model-version in request and add seed/logging in telemetry

Quickstart snippets (minimal, copy-paste)
- JS (node):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
  const stream = client.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-compact-v1', prompt: 'Explain recursion in 3 lines' })
  for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk.text) }

- Python:
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
  resp = c.generate(model='redwood-compact-v1', prompt='Explain recursion in 3 lines')
  print(resp.text)

Observability checklist for the first demo
- Confirm SDK emits sdk.request.start and sdk.request.end events to local dev console
- Confirm request shows model and sdk_version in traces
- Confirm an example 401 and 429 appear in Sentry/Tracing playground code path

Prompt lab: 3 quick pattern checks to include in quickstart
- Anchoring: prepend "You are a concise assistant." to prompts as a default template
- Context window sanity: show token count for sample prompt and warn if >80% of default max
- Structured output: demo function-calling style with 1 function and parse JSON fallback

Acceptance criteria for merging quickstart into main docs
- One-click run: npm/pip install, set key, run hello script -> success on CI (smoke test)
- Telemetry contract implemented and feature-flagged off by default
- Minimal troubleshooting guide included (the triage checklist above)
- Example demonstrates both streaming and non-streaming paths

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide default sampling rate for telemetry in prod (1% vs 5%) and how to surface in Console
- CI smoke: do we run a live call in CI or a replayed mock? (security + flakiness tradeoffs)
- Provide a one-command sandbox that repros a 429 using a local throttling proxy for demos

References & links
- GH PR for telemetry interface: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter/pull/89
- UX note: slack thread #sdk-onramp (ref: thread id 3421)
- Related Confluence: SDK Onramp Principles (linked above)

Quick notes for docs writer (when converting to long-form Quickstart)
- Keep persona callouts at top of each section (explicitly label assays: "3-min frontend", "5-min backend")
- Use screenshots sparingly — prefer gifs for streaming token demo
- Add a detachable 'telemetry appendix' that shows sample JSON payloads and opt-out instructions

Small list of immediate action items (owners)
- Taylor: wire telemetry interface into JS SDK (owner) — due 2025-01-20
- Aisha: write CI smoke wrapper and sandbox proxy recipe (owner) — due 2025-01-28
- Marcus: draft quickstart page copy + gifs (owner) — due 2025-02-02

End of draft.
